steps.name: QC and paired DESeq2 model fit
caveats: Verify sample-column-to-metadata mapping explicitly rather than assuming order matches; a silent mismatch on a paired design corrupts every downstream contrast
With only 4 subjects per condition, dispersion estimates are noisy — rely on DESeq2's default shrinkage rather than gene-wise estimates alone
Check for and report any subject-condition combination that is missing, since the paired design assumes complete blocks
steps.question: Do the raw Salmon gene counts (12000 genes x 12 samples, 4 subjects x {control, treated_a, treated_b}) support a paired DESeq2 design (~subject + condition), and what are the size factors / dispersion diagnostics?
acceptance_criteria: Counts and metadata are loaded and sample identifiers in counts.csv columns are matched one-to-one to metadata.csv rows
A DESeqDataSet is built with design ~subject + condition, subject and condition both encoded as factors with control as the reference level of condition
Low-count genes are filtered (e.g. rowSums or per-group minimum count filter) before running DESeq
Size factors, dispersion estimates, and a PCA or sample-distance plot (colored by subject and by condition) are produced and saved
The fitted DESeqDataSet object is saved to disk for reuse by downstream contrast-extraction steps

steps.name: Extract treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control, and treated_a vs treated_b contrasts
caveats: LFC shrinkage (apeglm) requires the coefficient to be named exactly as it appears in resultsNames(dds); confirm names before calling lfcShrink
The treated_a vs treated_b contrast answers whether the treatments differ from each other directly — do not substitute an indirect comparison of the two vs-control contrasts for this
With n=4 per condition, statistical power is limited; report this explicitly rather than treating a lack of significance as evidence of no effect
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed for treated_a vs control, for treated_b vs control, and directly for treated_a vs treated_b, controlling for subject in a within-subject paired design?
acceptance_criteria: Three Wald contrasts are extracted from the single fitted model in T1S1: treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control, treated_a vs treated_b
Each contrast's results table reports log2FoldChange, shrunken LFC (via apeglm or ashr shrinkage), p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value, joined back to gene symbol
Results tables for all three contrasts are exported as CSV with gene symbols preserved
Significance thresholds (padj < 0.05, |log2FC| > 1 as a default reportable cutoff, explicitly stated) are applied and counts of significant genes per contrast are reported
An MA plot and a volcano plot are generated for each of the three contrasts

steps.name: Union of treatment-responsive genes and concordance/discordance classification
caveats: A gene absent from the direct A-vs-B contrast's significant list can still differ numerically between treatments if effect sizes are similar but each individually crosses the vs-control threshold — the concordant/discordant labeling from vs-control contrasts alone is not equivalent to formally testing A vs B, which is why the direct contrast is also reported per gene
steps.question: Which genes respond to either treatment relative to control (union of the treated_a-vs-control and treated_b-vs-control significant gene sets), and among those, which show concordant (same-direction) versus discordant or treatment-differential (significant in the direct treated_a vs treated_b contrast) responses?
acceptance_criteria: A gene-level table is built taking the union of genes significant (padj < 0.05) in either treated_a-vs-control or treated_b-vs-control from T1S2
Each gene in the union is annotated with its significance status and log2FC sign in all three contrasts

Genes are classified into categories: concordant (significant, same-direction LFC in both vs-control contrasts), A-specific (significant only for A), B-specific (significant only for B), and treatment-differential (significant in the direct A-vs-B contrast, flagged regardless of the vs-control pattern)
A summary table with counts per category and the full classified gene list are exported as CSV
A Venn diagram or UpSet-style plot of the treated_a-vs-control and treated_b-vs-control significant gene sets is produced

steps.name: Pathway enrichment per contrast using WikiPathways human gene sets
caveats: Gene symbols in counts.csv must match the HGNC symbol convention used in the WikiPathways GMT; report any join loss (genes present in the DE table but absent from the pathway gene universe)
With only 4 subjects per condition, per-gene p-values driving the rank are themselves noisy, so treat enrichment results as hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory
steps.question: Which WikiPathways human pathways are enriched among genes differentially expressed for treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control, and treated_a vs treated_b?
acceptance_criteria: WikiPathways human GMT gene sets (HGNC symbols) are loaded from the reference store and pathway names are recovered by splitting the '%'-delimited descriptor field
For each of the three contrasts from T1S2, a pre-ranked GSEA (ranking by signed -log10(p) x sign(log2FC) or by the Wald statistic) is run against the WikiPathways gene sets
Enrichment results (NES, p-value, BH-adjusted p-value, leading-edge genes) are exported as CSV per contrast

Top enriched pathways (adjusted p < 0.25 for GSEA, as conventional) are reported for each contrast, and pathways enriched in both vs-control contrasts versus only one are flagged for interpretive relevance to whether the treatments converge or diverge mechanistically
If the WikiPathways human reference is unavailable at run time, the step reports the gap explicitly rather than substituting an unmatched-organism gene set

plan.title: Paired 3-condition DE: treatment A/B vs control in blood
plan.analytical_narrative: The design is 4 subjects each sampled under control, treated_a, and treated_b — a paired, within-subject repeated-measures design over 12000 genes x 13 columns (12 samples + gene symbol). This calls for a single DESeq2 model with subject as a blocking factor and condition (control/treated_a/treated_b) as the factor of interest, so that each treatment-vs-control contrast removes inter-subject variability, followed by a direct treated_a vs treated_b contrast to test whether the two treatments differ from each other. Because DESeq2's Wald contrasts from one fitted paired model are more powerful and more comparable than three independent pairwise tests, we fit one design (~subject + condition) and pull out all three contrasts (A vs control, B vs control, A vs B) from it. Genes 'responding to either treatment' are then defined as the union of significant genes from the two vs-control contrasts. We follow DE with pathway enrichment on each contrast's gene list using WikiPathways human gene sets (the organism-matched reference available in this environment), and finish with a comparison step that classifies genes into concordant (same direction, both treatments), discordant (opposite direction or A-only/B-only), and treatment-differential (significant in the direct A vs B contrast) categories to directly answer whether the treatments diverge.
